17-13-0303-C(1) Substitute Type 1 Narrative & Plans - 4639 South Wallace Street, Chicago,
IL

Proposed Zoning: B2-3 Neighborhood Mixed-Use District
Lot Area: 8,472.5 sq. ft.

Proposed Land Use: The Applicant is proposing to redevelop the subject property with a new
four-story mixed-use building and a one-story detached garage. The
proposed building will measure 47 ft.-0.875 inches in height and will
contain 10,180 sq. ft. of commercial space floors 1 and 2, which will be
occupied by a daycare facility. There will be six (6) dwelling units on floors
3 through 4. The subject property is a Transit Served Location. Pursuant to
Sec. 17-13-0303-D optional Administrative Adjustment and Variation and
pursuant to Secs. 17-13-1003-EE and 17-13-1101-B of the Chicago Zoning
Ordinance, the Applicant is seeking to reduce the off-street parking
requirement for a Transit Served Location to six (6) parking spaces, reduce
the front yard setback from 10 ft. to 10 inches, reduce the north side setback
to from 5 fi. to 4 inches, reduce the south side setback from 5 ft. to 4 ft.,
and seeking all relief necessary, as allowed by the code, for the Type 1 plan
set.

(A) The Project’s Floor Area Ratio: 19,350 square feet (2.82 FAR)

(B) The Project’s Density (Minimum Lot Area Per D.U.): 1,412.08 square feet per D.U.
(6 residential units)
(C) The amount of off-street parking: 6 parking spaces

*The subject property is a designated Transit Served Location (47" Street CTA Bus
Line Corridor Roadway Segment). Pursuant to Sec. 17-13-1003-EE, the Applicant
is seeking to reduce the required number of off-street parking spaces from twelve
(12) parking spaces to six (6) parking spaces.

(D) — Setbacks:
a. *Front Setback: 0 ft.-10 inches (proposed)
db. *Side Setbacks:
North Side: 0 ft.-4 inches (proposed)
South Side: 4 ft. (proposed)
c. Rear Setback: 42 ft.-2 inches (proposed)

*Pursuant to Sec. 17-13-1101-B, the Applicant is seeking to reduce the front yard
setback from 10 ft. to 10 inches, reduce the north side setback to from 5 ft. to 4
inches, reduce the south side setback from 5 ft. to 4 ft.

(E) Building Height: 47 ft.-0.875 inches

Sec. 17-3-0308 Criteria for Transit-Served Locations — Substitute Supplemental Narrative Zoning
Analysis

1. The subject property is a designated Transit Served Location per Sec. 17-10-0102-B
because it is located within approximately 290 linear feet of the 47" Street CTA Bus Line
Corridor roadway segment. The proposed mixed-use building containing 10,180 sq. ft. of
commercial space, for a daycare facility, on the 1* and 2™ floors and six (6) residential
units above will be supported by six (6) off-street parking spaces and ten (10) bicycle
parking spaces. Pursuant to Section 17-13-1003-EE, the Applicant is seeking to permit a
decrease in the number of required off-street parking spaces from twelve (12) parking
spaces to six (6) parking spaces.

2. The proposed building design complies with the main building door and entryway design
standards provided by Sec. 17-4-0504. The proposed building will have a front setback of
10 inches from the subject lot’s front property line along South Wallace Street to align with
the footprints of the neighboring buildings on the block. The building’s first floor was
designed with windows facing the sidewalk located along South Wallace Street.

3. The Transit Friendly Development Guide defines ‘transit friendly development’ as
development which is oriented towards and integrated with adjacent transit. The proposed
mixed-use building incorporates accessibility and connectivity to mass transit based on its
location near the 47" Street CTA bus route. The Applicant believes the project will
improve a lot located along South Wallace Street for residents and other commuters
traveling in the subject area.

4. The proposed mixed-use building will contain commercial uses on floors 1 and 2, which
will be occupied by a daycare facility. There will be six (6) residential units on floors 3
through 4. The proposed building will be supported by six (6) off-street parking spaces and
ten (10) bicycle parking spaces. The Applicant is seeking administrative approval to permit
the off-street parking decrease pursuant to the eTOD Ordinance.

5. The Applicant believes the proposed mixed-use building will provide appropriate density
in the subject neighborhood, More specifically, the project will replace two (2) older
residential buildings with a new mixed-use building, which will provide additional
residential housing thereby meeting market demand. Based on the subject property’s
proximity to a designated CTA bus route (47" Street CTA Bus Line), the Applicant
believes the project provides transit options and otherwise complies with the Travel
Demand Study and Management Plan rules promulgated by the Department of
Transportation by serving an area in need. a
